utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Ms. Sartorio, you're appearing for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I represent General Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very. We're dealing today with a Status Conference in the case of the Prosecutor against Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac. The accused have indicated that they do not wish to be present for those proceedings today, so we proceed in their absence. This is the third Status Conference, the last being on the 12th of October. And I understand that in preparation for this, there was a 65 ter Conference yesterday with the parties and the senior legal officer of the Trial Chamber. The first matter to ask is whether there are any issues concerning the health of either accused which could be relevant to the ongoing preparation of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, General Cermak has no health problems. During his stay in detention, he actually recovered fully. That may sound a bit contradictory, but that's actually the way it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, I think that sometimes happens. A quiet rest, yes. Mr. Separovic, any problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no special problems. Blood sugar is a constant problem, but the fact that he was released contributed to an improvement in his condition, so there's nothing special I have to add. He goes for regular checkups, and his health condition is the way it was before, except that his blood sugar is down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear that from each of the counsel. Perhaps it's the counsel we'll have to care for rather than the accused in getting this case ready for trial. Matters pending, the only matter of which I'm aware is the decision in the final stages of preparation on the indictment and which will be delivered shortly. Matters of disclosure. I understand that the Rule 66(A)(i) is now complete. Is that right, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Rule 66(A)(ii), where is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were going at the last conference to disclose by November some 4 to 500 additional documents, and some 10 additional international witness statements, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's been done. Since the last Status Conference on the 12th of October, we have made three sets of disclosure, and all of the witness statements have been disclosed to date, and -- as well as most of the 66(A) documents. However, as you know, disclosure is ongoing, and there will be additional witnesses and documents that will come up. But as of this date, we've complied with Rule 66(A).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, is there any other aspect of disclosure that is still ongoing at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. It's always ongoing, the review. And as we go along, we intend to make disclosure on a rolling basis. And in addition, we have disclosed all Rule 66 -- 68(I) materials for which we have actual knowledge and for which we have reviewed. And again on a continuing, ongoing rolling basis, as we review documents and take additional witness statements, we will be disclosing those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I can produce some statistics for Your Honours, numbers of documents, if you wish, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. As long as you see no particular problem there, I don't think the record will feel upset if it doesn't get a whole lot of statistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, though. Now, I understand, and I'll address this to all counsel, that there may be some problem with the electronic disclosure system, a technical problem affecting Defence counsel. Is it something that you need to say something about, Mr. Prodanovic or Mr. Separovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything that my colleague from the Prosecution said is quite correct. They did submit these documents to us. However, we have some technical problems in terms of opening the material and reading it. We didn't manage to open some documents at all; on others, we had little Xs or whatever, and yet others we didn't manage to find at all. Yesterday, after the meeting, we realised that the system functions properly here in The Hague, in the building; however, the problem lies in the Internet connections in Croatia. They are not stable. When we open big materials, I mean a large number of pages, then we have such problems. We agreed that we would have to enhance our technical capabilities, get better Internet. And we think that that is the way of dealing with this problem. We tried to deal with this yesterday, here in the building, and we realised that the system was fine here but that the problem, obviously, lay with the Internet connections in Croatia. So that's it. If we do not succeed, we will probably have to address the Chamber, asking them to perhaps order the Prosecution to give us these materials on CD, so that our clients, who are not very well-versed in such matters, could become familiar with the material, and we too. We believe that with faster Internet, this problem will have been resolved. However, I must say that we had major problems with reading these materials in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, by the sound of what you say, Mr. Separovic, it would be a matter for liaison between yourselves and the technical people here in The Hague, probably from Croatia, so that you can discuss the problem as it's happening and hopefully identify with greater accuracy what it is that needs to be either adjusted or replaced with something different, to enable you to get a reliable access. It ought to work. So that if some liaison can identify the problem and get it corrected, that will make life a lot easier for all of you, won't it? If it's something beyond that, of course you'll have to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I assume there will be full cooperation in that respect with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I have made inquiries myself with Mr. Bob Reid, the Deputy -- Chief of Investigations, and he is going to be meeting with OLAD and others to ensure that the proper assistance is provided to the Defence attorneys. And in addition, I've spoken with the person who is specifically appointed to work with Defence attorneys on such matters, as problems with EDS, and he is committed as well to ensuring that they get the proper assistance and training that they need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. The important thing will be to try and identify whatever is the technical problem and get that remedied as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Rule 70 disclosure, that's still alive, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, and we have sent out requests in over 500 -- for over 500 documents for permission to disclose those documents. We are still awaiting decisions. We expect to have decisions and disclosure made by our deadline, which is the 28th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honour, just to correct earlier when we discussed Rule 66(A)(ii), we have, as you my, chronic problem with translations, and many of the statements have not yet been translated. But we have made requests, and we are going to encourage the Translation Unit to, as much as they can, put our witness statements through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You were going to provide copies of the interviews with the accused, were you not? Where is that at?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We did that, Your Honour. Two days after the Status Conference, we provided all the transcripts. Yesterday, Mr. Separovic, who represents Mr. Markac, stated that he did not receive it, the statement of Mr. Markac. Our records show that his co-counsel, Mr. Mikulicic, had signed it, but as a courtesy result we provided Mr. Separovic a copy of it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that should overcome any hitch there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you at the moment, apart from the business of getting statements translated, you're seeing no problems with disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And from the Defence point of view, the big problem is to get the technical difficulty overcome so that you can get reliable access to what is being made available. All right. Agreed facts. Where have we got to with that, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we have been concentrating mainly on disclosure for the last three or four months, and I think we're in a position now to turn to drafting some agreed facts and submitting them to the Defence attorneys. And I know that Mr. Scott, the senior trial attorney, and I are committed to doing that within the next couple of months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So nothing has been provided yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That seems to be all the technical matters that I need to inquire into. Is there any other general matter that you need to raise, Ms. Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: None at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, is there any particular issue that you need to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing arising, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Separovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. I understand from the senior legal officer that there was an inquiry made about the terms of the conditions under which the two accused are released. I notice that in paragraph 44 of the decision of the Appeals Chamber, subparagraph A, item 10, it's set out that they are not to have any contact with each other or with any other accused before this Tribunal. As I understood from the senior legal officer, the query was whether the two accused were free to deal with each other. Under the present order of the Appeals Chamber, the answer is no. If that is a particular difficulty, there would need to be an application brought to try to vary those terms, and there would have to be justification offered for any such variation. If I understand correctly from the senior legal officer, there's also a question whether it might be possible to go some little distance to a place of business or work. Again, under the terms of the present order of the Appeals Chamber, that's not possible, so that if that is desired, it will, again, be necessary to bring an application to vary the terms upon which the Appeals Chamber has ordered provisional release. I mention those two things in case that would assist Defence counsel in understanding the position. And the application would be made to Trial Chamber II for any variation that is sought. It would be in writing, with the justification. The Office of the Prosecutor would be able to respond. And then Trial Chamber II would reach a decision whether there could be any variation in the present conditions of provisional release. If there are no other matters, that concludes this conference. I thank everybody for their attendance.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
